name: BONECLOCK: Shelf Death Pool & Survival Market
description: BONECLOCK is the Shelf's most notorious underground prediction market, where bettors wager on the survival timelines of known figures — gang lieutenants, corrupt block wardens, augment-debt enforcers, and the occasional Tier 3 bureaucrat who wandered too far south. Operated by a rotating cell of bookmakers known only as the Clockface Syndicate, the market runs through encrypted mesh nodes embedded in decommissioned water-treatment infrastructure beneath the Tier 1 stack, accepting anonymous Quanta transfers in denominations as low as Φ0.50. The operation has survived three Axiom enforcement sweeps by migrating its ledger architecture mid-raid, and its odds — updated every six hours — are considered grimly accurate enough that Shelf residents sometimes use a subject's BONECLOCK line as a proxy for neighborhood safety assessments.
story_hooks: A runner discovers their own name has appeared on BONECLOCK with rapidly shortening odds — someone with access to information they shouldn't have is betting on their imminent death, and tracing the position back through the Clockface Syndicate's encrypted nodes means navigating a market that profits from not answering questions.

A Tier 3 social researcher embeds in the Shelf to study BONECLOCK as an informal risk-assessment institution, only to realize the Syndicate has opened a position on her — not as a death threat, but as a test of whether she'll buy herself out or report them, which will tell them everything they need to know about whether she's safe to keep alive.

The Clockface Syndicate's lead bookmaker wants out and is willing to hand over the full encrypted ledger — three years of positions, payouts, and the identities of every high-tier bettor who quietly accessed the market through anonymized proxies — to whoever can get her family off the Shelf first.
